prompt: Write a short blog post about what comes next for your digital team. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
# What Comes Next for Our Digital Team

Every team reaches a point where the work that got it here stops being the work that carries it forward. For our digital team, that point is now.

Over the past year we've focused on building: launching new features, stabilizing our infrastructure, and getting our processes to a place where they're dependable. That foundation matters. But a foundation isn't the finished house, and the next chapter is about what we build on top of it.

## Fewer handoffs, faster learning

The biggest drag on any digital team is waiting: for approvals, for another team's review, for a release window. Over the coming months we're reorganizing around small, cross-functional groups that own an outcome from idea to measurement. Designers, engineers, and analysts will sit together instead of passing work down a line. We expect to ship smaller changes more often, and to learn from each one before deciding what to do next.

## AI as a teammate, not a headline

We're past the stage of asking whether AI belongs in our workflow. The better question is where it genuinely helps. We're putting assistants to work on the unglamorous parts: drafting tests, triaging bug reports, summarizing user feedback, and catching accessibility problems early. People stay accountable for decisions and quality. The goal is to give everyone more time for the judgment calls that only they can make.

## Measuring what matters

We've tracked plenty of numbers, but not all of them told us something useful. This year we're trimming our dashboards down to a handful of measures tied directly to customer outcomes: how quickly people accomplish what they came to do, how often they come back, and where they get stuck. If a metric doesn't change a decision, it goes.

## Investing in the people

None of this works without a team that feels trusted and equipped. We're setting aside dedicated time for learning, rotating people across projects to broaden skills, and making it easier to raise concerns early. Sustainable pace is a feature, not a perk.

## What you can expect

Expect some turbulence. Reorganizing teams, changing tools, and rethinking metrics will not all go smoothly, and we'll get some things wrong. We'll share what we learn along the way, including the missteps.

If you're a customer, you'll notice improvements arriving more steadily. If you're a colleague, you'll see clearer ownership and fewer meetings. And if you're thinking about joining us, this is a good time to do it.

We'll report back in a few months with results. Until then, we're heads down and building.
